title: 16.1 Tomahawk5: 51.2Tb/s 5nm Monolithic Switch Chip for AI/ML Networking
problem: Next-generation data center and AI networks demand switching capacity beyond previous generation (25.6Tb/s); monolithic integration at scale requires advanced SerDes technology supporting diverse optical/copper connectivity options while achieving 51.2Tb/s in 5nm.
motivation: Explosive growth in AI/ML workloads and data center interconnect demands create need for next-generation high-capacity, flexible switch architectures.
method: Tomahawk5 is a monolithic chip—meaning all the network switching logic fits on one 5-nanometer piece of silicon—achieving 51.2 trillion bits per second switching capacity in a single integrated design. The chip uses Peregrine SerDes cores, which are high-speed circuits that translate signals between the chip's internal architecture and external cables, enabling it to work with multiple physical connection formats. These cores support direct copper cables, front-panel optics, pluggable optical modules, and fiber optics built directly into the chip's package, allowing data centers to use whichever connection method they already have deployed.
key_novelty: Embedding Peregrine SerDes cores into the monolithic switch enables a single 51.2Tb/s chip to natively support multiple connection types—copper and various optical formats—without needing separate interface cards.
contributions: 5nm monolithic integration for data center AI/ML
primary_theme: High-capacity monolithic switch for AI/ML data centers
